subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: What user-visible identifier policy should OpenClaw use when showing context-overflow diagnostics across channels?
rationale: The code can already compute useful token/model/session facts, but exposing raw session keys, channel IDs, or provider/model details affects privacy, supportability, and consistency across Discord, webchat, and other channels.

options.title: Use redacted display labels
options.body: Show a safe channel/session display label plus provider/model, effective limit, observed or estimated size, overage, and recovery actions through a shared formatter.

options.title: Keep raw IDs out of chat
options.body: Keep chat messages generic and expose the detailed facts only in logs, status, or diagnostic bundles.

options.title: Split warning UX separately
options.body: Limit this issue to terminal overflow errors and track proactive threshold warnings or response footers in a separate context-visibility item.

recommendation.title: Use redacted display labels
recommendation.body: Show a safe channel/session display label plus provider/model, effective limit, observed or estimated size, overage, and recovery actions through a shared formatter.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has current-main history on the central runner/fallback paths and already framed the prior review around the same product boundary.
